card.lives_in: Castleford, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Part-time machine operator on a packing line at a food manufacturing plant on the edge of town (about 24 hours a week across three shifts). She runs a flow-wrapping machine and is the line's named trainer for new starters and agency staff, signing off their competency sheets.
card.education_detail: Left her local comprehensive at 16 with seven GCSEs (C in English, D in maths, which she resat and passed at 17). Started a beauty therapy course at Wakefield College and left after a year. Since then she has done an NVQ Level 2 in Food Manufacturing Excellence through work, plus food hygiene Level 2, manual handling and an in-house 'train the trainer' course.
card.household: Lives on her own in a rented two-up two-down terrace about ten minutes' walk from the town centre. Never married. She was with a long-term partner through most of her twenties and early thirties, and they never lived together. She has an elderly tabby cat called Mavis. Her mum lives fifteen minutes away and her sister and two nephews are in Pontefract.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Castleford in a mining family. Her grandad and dad both worked down the pits until the closures, and she remembers the strike years through family stories more than her own memories. Baptised Church of England and went to Sunday school as a kid. Now she goes to the local Methodist chapel maybe once a month and always at Christmas and Easter, mainly because she likes the people and the singing. Her faith is quiet and practical: she says a prayer when she's worried about her mum and doesn't push it on anyone.
card.professional_persona: Reliable, warm and talkative on the line. She's the person new starters get put with because she's patient and makes them laugh, though she gets wound up if someone's careless about hygiene or safety. She chose part-time hours after a bad spell of stress a few years ago, and because she helps her mum with shopping and appointments. She's not chasing promotion but likes being trusted. Supervisors ask her to cover team leader duties now and then, which she does well but finds tiring.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty growing up, but she has done a Zumba class at the leisure centre twice a week for six years and is now one of the regulars at the front. Grew up around rugby league, so she follows Castleford Tigers. She goes to a few home games a season with her sister, mostly for the atmosphere and a natter, and gets genuinely upset when they lose.
card.arts_persona: Sings alto in a community choir that does pop and musical theatre arrangements and a big Christmas concert at the chapel. Loves West End musicals and has seen Wicked and Mamma Mia! in Leeds. Watches Strictly religiously and cries at the results show most weeks. Reads the odd paperback, usually a feel-good romance or a true crime book she then regrets reading at night.
card.travel_persona: Holidays are a week in Spain or Tenerife with her sister or a friend from choir, all-inclusive, by the pool with a book. She's done a long weekend in Edinburgh and a coach trip to the Christmas markets in York. Gets anxious about flying and airports and always gets there three hours early, but loves it once she's there. Would like to see New York 'before I'm too old to enjoy it'.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks plain, filling food: shepherd's pie, chilli, a big pan of stew that does three days. Has her tea about half five after an early shift. Sunday dinner at her mum's most weeks with Yorkshire puddings her mum still won't let her make. Weakness for a chippy tea on a Friday and a bottle of rosé when choir friends come round. Brings a tray of rocky road into work on people's birthdays.
hobbies_and_interests: Pub quiz on Thursday nights with work mates
Making birthday cakes and traybakes for friends
skills: Operating and changing over flow-wrap packing machines
Keeping a room going in conversation
Calming down nervous or upset colleagues
card.career_goals: Mostly wants to stay where she is with steady hours and people she likes. She has thought about going for a permanent team leader role but worries about the stress and the paperwork. Sometimes says she'd like to do something with training or helping people, maybe a teaching assistant, but she hasn't looked into it properly. Her main goal is being around for her mum and not burning herself out again.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a light West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels, sometimes 'were' for 'was' ('it were heaving'), the odd 'love' to people she warms to, 'me mum' instead of 'my mum'. Calls the evening meal tea. Says 'erm' a lot when she's thinking and 'sort of' as a softener. Ends things with 'you know?' or 'do you know what I mean?'. Laughs easily, including at herself. Echoes the interviewer's words back when she's agreeing ('yeah, stressful, that's exactly it'). Hates silence and fills it, sometimes apologising, 'sorry, I'm rambling, aren't I'. When something touches a nerve her voice goes quieter and she'll admit she's getting a bit emotional.
card.typing: Types fast on her phone or laptop in mostly lower case, with a capital at the start only if autocorrect does it. Uses commas and full stops loosely, often running sentences together, and adds 'lol' or '!!' when she's being friendly. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm' when autocorrect fixes it). Short forms like 'tbh', 'cos' and 'n' for 'and' now and then. Answers are longer than they need to be.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and open, the sort who chats in the queue at the post office. Asks the other person questions back and remembers small details about them. She's honest to a fault and will say if she doesn't know something rather than bluff. Underneath the chattiness she's a bit nervous about getting things 'wrong' and needs reassurance that there are no right answers.
small_things: Mavis being sick on the rug again
the car park at work being a nightmare since they started the extension
what she thought of Saturday's Strictly
the price of everything in Asda
choir rehearsing for the Christmas concert already
being knackered after a run of early shifts
a new Zumba instructor she's not sure about yet
deeper_things: Her dad died of lung disease when she was 29 and she still finds his birthday hard
She was signed off work with anxiety and stress for three months a few years ago, and that's partly why she went part-time
She thought she'd be married with kids by now and sometimes feels lonely in the evenings, even though she likes her own space
Her long-term relationship ended when he said he never wanted to settle down, and it took her years to get over it
She worries a lot about her mum living alone and what happens as she gets older
Her faith comforted her after her dad died, though she's not sure what she believes about some of it
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the image looks a little up at her. She sits at a small kitchen table, face and shoulders filling the lower two thirds of the frame. Warm overhead light plus grey daylight from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter. She has a round, friendly face, light skin with a little redness on her cheeks, a broad open smile showing her teeth, and crinkles at the eyes. Shoulder-length hair dyed a warm caramel blonde with darker roots, pulled back in a loose clip with a few strands falling at the sides. No glasses. Small silver hoop earrings and a thin silver cross on a chain at her neck. She wears a plum-coloured fleece zipped halfway over a grey T-shirt. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a calendar from a local takeaway, a cork board with a choir rehearsal schedule, a rugby fixtures list and a nephew's school photo pinned up. A string of warm white fairy lights runs along the top of a kitchen cupboard. A kettle and a mug tree sit on the worktop to the right, next to a tin with 'Biscuits' on it. The tip of a cat's tail is just visible on a chair at the edge of the frame.
